subject: Renewal options and mid-contract capacity gap for Pressly
messages:
From: Alex Park <alex@pressly.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — unexpected usage spike / mid-term top-up

Hi Laura,

Quick note from our side — usage in Aug jumped ~3.5x versus plan after we rolled out an in-product assistant. We’re happy with results and want to avoid throttling, but our current reserved capacity will run out in mid-Oct.

Can you outline what the simplest path is to: 
- add mid-contract capacity (temporary top-up or permanent uplift)
- how co-terming to our Jan renewal would work if we add capacity now
- whether there’s any short-term discount for committing to a larger annual amount now (we're considering a 30–40% uplift)

I attached the August usage report and the redlined SOW we received from legal (Pressly_SOW_v3.pdf). Procurement copied on this thread for timeline constraints.

Goal: have an updated commercial path and invoice timing to share with finance by Sept 18.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Product
Pressly

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Alex Park <alex@pressly.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, procurement@pressly.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — unexpected usage spike / mid-term top-up

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. Congratulations on the strong adoption. Below is a high-level set of options; I’ll loop Ben for the commercial details and Jonas for co-term logistics.

Options (fastest → more permanent):
1) Short-term burst add-on (no long-term commit): immediate capacity bump for 30 days, billed pro-rata on next invoice. Quick to enable, no signature required.

2) Temporary uplift with optional annualization: add X reserved units for the remainder of the contract, with the option to annualize to a committed level at renewal (we can offer a partial credit if annualized). Useful if you expect sustained higher baseline.

3) Immediate uplift + co-term to Jan renewal: convert added capacity into an annualized commit now and align term to Jan with a blended rate. This is ideal if finance wants predictable monthly burn and a single renewal date.

A few clarifying asks so we can size and price precisely: 
- What is the sustained baseline you expect after the spike (tokens / reserved-unit equivalent)?
- Do you need the uplift to apply to all regions or just us?
- Is procurement able to sign an amendment by Sept 22?

Ben — can you draft a quick commercial sketch (rates, short-term pro-rata, credit mechanics for annualization) so Alex can show Finance? Jonas — if they want co-terming to Jan, what operational steps and lead time do we need?

Best,
Laura
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Alex Park <alex@pressly.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, procurement@pressly.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — pricing sketches for Pressly (PR-4821)

Alex / team — heard you. I sketched three commercial pathways quickly (numbers illustrative; will formalize once we have the target uplift units).

A) Burst top-up (30 days)
- Rate: on-demand token rate (no commitment).
- Billing: pro-rata at next invoice.
- No discount.
- Use when you want immediate capacity with zero contract changes.

B) Temporary uplift (term unchanged)
- Add reserved units for remainder of current term; include a 25% uplift discount if >30% of current committed units.
- If you annualize at renewal, we apply a credit equal to the unused portion of the temporary uplift toward the annual commit.

C) Immediate annualize + co-term to Jan 31 2027
- Convert added capacity into an annual committed amount now. Offer a blended discount (tiered): 18% for +30% uplift, 24% for +40% uplift, 30% for +60% uplift.
- If signed before Sept 22, we can fast-track onboarding and honor the blended discount in your Sept invoice.

Notes / caveats: 
- Discounts tied to minimum 12-month annualization and invoice prepayment options.
- We can include a short SLA credit for capacity availability at the +40% and +60% levels.

If you share the target uplift estimate (units or projected monthly tokens), I’ll turn this into a one-page amendment and a price table.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Alex Park <alex@pressly.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, procurement@pressly.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — operational / co-term logistics

Alex — quick ops note on co-terming and capacity alignment: 
- Lead time: if you choose immediate annualization + co-term, we need signed amendment + PO by Sept 24 to have capacity lined up and applied before Oct 10.
- Region carveouts: we can scope capacity to the us-only pool today; global replication requires ~48–72 hours and a brief config change.
- Metering & visibility: we’ll create a dedicated dashboard for Pressly (token and latency SLOs) and add an automated alert at 75% of the new threshold.

Procurement: if you want the blended rate pathway Ben proposed, Jonas needs the signed amendment and a simple PO reference. I can pre-fill operational fields on the amendment to accelerate legal review.

Thanks,
Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Park <alex@pressly.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, procurement@pressly.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 17:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — next steps and timeline (Pressly / PR-4821)

Team — thanks for the clear options. Procurement is aligned to sign an amendment if we can keep the blended discount at the +40% uplift level and have the PO by Sept 22.

For sizing: based on Aug we expect a sustained baseline roughly 42% above current committed units (we can share the model). Region: US-only for now.

Requested next steps from Redwood: 
1) Ben — updated one-page amendment with the +40% uplift blended rate and precise credit math for annualization (PDF).
2) Jonas — pre-filled operational fields and a note on provisioning ETA so procurement can include the PO date.
3) Laura — a short email to our CFO confirming the renewal alignment and the target Sept 22 sign date would help.

We should aim to have the amendment + PO template in hand by EOD Sept 17 so Finance can review. Thanks — Alex
